decisions.quote: The visual inspections which supported these analyses are not fully confirmed statistically. Considering that only two possible dividing responses were permitted (equal or unequal), the verification of contingency control over these responses depends on the confirmation that the correct responses proportion was above 50%. In G1, the total proportion of correct divisions after each winning round was 63.4% (Z=2.43; p=0.008). This higher proportion was confirmed in both contingencies (Contingency A: 60.4%, Z=2.07 p=0.019; Contingency B: 67.7%, Z= 2.89 p=0.002). In G2 and G3 the proportion of “+” signs subsequent to winnings was 58.0% and 55.1% respectively, but they were not statistically superior to 50% considering α=0.05 (G2: Z=1.44, p=0.074; G3: Z=0.91, p=0.182). Controlling relations of earnings over division responses were confirmed for both G2 and G3 under contingency B (G2: Z=2.42, p=0.007 and G3: Z=2.92, p=0.002). However, statistical significance was not reached when they were under contingency A.
decisions.reason: Although all groups reached the contingency-change criterion as in Vichi et al. (2009), the authors qualify that visual inspection was not fully confirmed statistically: controlling relations were statistically significant across both contingencies in only one group (G1), whereas in the other two groups (G2 and G3) control was confirmed only under Contingency B and not Contingency A.

blind_target.authors: Vichi, C., Andery, M. A. P. A., & Glenn, S. S.
blind_target.title: A Metacontingency Experiment: The Effects of Contingent Consequences on Patterns of Interlocking Contingencies of Reinforcement.
blind_target.evidence_quote: Given the importance of the investigative proposal made by Vichi et al. (2009), a new replication of this procedure was conducted to examine if, despite the differences between the studied groups, the experimental variables manipulated would select collective behaviors (IBCs).
blind_target.outcome_quote: If, as in Vichi et al (2009) and Lopes (2010), the study considers only if successive gains reached the criterion for contingency change, then we can state that the data here obtained replicated the ones from Vichi et al. and disagree with the ones from Lopes, since all groups reached these criteria. In this sense, the contingencies here manipulated established control over collective behaviors, being an experimental analogous to metacontingencies.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly report replication using the original successive-gain criterion. Their additional statistical analysis is qualified as noncomparable because the original did not conduct it; it is not a stated failed comparison with the original.
